sample_test_cases.explanation: The longest consecutive sequence is [1,2,3,4], which has length 4.

hints: Sorting solves the problem but does not meet the O(n) requirement.
Fast existence lookup is the key.
Only start counting a sequence when the previous number is not present.
Use a HashSet to check whether numbers exist in constant time.
explanation: Store all numbers in a HashSet for O(1) lookups. For each number, check whether it is the start of a sequence by verifying that the previous number does not exist in the set. If it is a starting point, continue extending the sequence while consecutive numbers exist. Track the maximum sequence length found during the process and return it.

title: Group Shifted Strings
description: Given an array of lowercase strings, group all shifted strings together. A string can be shifted to another string by shifting every character forward by the same number of positions in the alphabet. Characters wrap around from 'z' to 'a'. Return the groups in any order.
constraints: strings[i] consists of lowercase English letters

sample_test_cases.explanation: Strings are grouped according to their shifting pattern.

hints: Two strings belong to the same group if their relative character differences are identical.
Convert each string into a normalized pattern.
A HashMap can group strings with the same pattern.
Remember that alphabet shifting wraps around from 'z' to 'a'.
explanation: For each string, create a signature representing the difference between consecutive characters. For example, 'abc' becomes '1,1' and 'bcd' also becomes '1,1'. Strings with the same signature belong to the same shifted group. Use a HashMap where the signature is the key and the value is the list of strings sharing that pattern.

title: Randomized Set
description: Design a data structure that supports insert, remove, and getRandom operations in average O(1) time. Implement the RandomizedSet class with the following methods: insert(val), remove(val), and getRandom(). Return the outputs of all operations except the constructor.
constraints: At most 200000 calls will be made
getRandom will only be called when the set is non-empty

sample_test_cases.explanation: Operations are executed in order while maintaining O(1) average complexity.

hints: A HashMap alone cannot support getRandom efficiently.
An array allows O(1) random access.
Store element positions in a HashMap.
When removing an element, swap it with the last element in the array before deleting.
explanation: Maintain both an array and a HashMap. The array stores all current elements, while the HashMap stores each element's index in the array. For insertion, append to the array and record the index. For deletion, swap the target element with the last element, update indices in the HashMap, and remove the last element. getRandom can then return a random element from the array in O(1) time.
